# Verification and refitting

## Verify the reconstructed results

~~~sh
Rscript verify_reproduction.R
~~~

The verifier compares reconstructed quantities with fixed references that the numerical build does not update. It checks the admitted simulation fit keys and common-dataset denominators, the direction of Gamma–Dual changes, Rasch score frequencies, interval endpoints, diagnostic gates and selected numeric claims. The G.2 calculation and the Table 2 and E.1 probabilities have independent checks. The reproduction map lists the validation path and evidence level for every one of the 62 current exhibits. [Reproduction map](records/reproduction-map.csv) · [Artifact contract](records/artifact-contract.csv) · [Calibration checks](code/verification/v104/methods.py) · [Simulation checks](code/verification/v104/simulation.py) · [Application checks](code/verification/v104/applications.py)

The simulation build includes the two selected posterior-CDF replay summaries. Application verification uses finite-CDF curves, density integrals, matched ranks and group averages from existing fits. A fresh fit answers a further question about sampling variability and convergence. A short executable example for each family is described below.

## Fit one simulation or application model

Check the `refit` dependencies before running a model. The following commands display the settings for one simulation fit, then run a short example:

~~~bash
Rscript refit/simulation/run_one_fit.R
Rscript refit/simulation/run_one_fit.R --profile smoke --execute
~~~

The default is a Gamma(1,1) fit with $J=25$, called Vague in the fit manifest. Use `--fit-key` from the fit-status manifest to select another model. The `smoke` profile uses 200 iterations with 100 discarded as warmup to check that the code runs. The `production` profile uses the original longer schedules and the four assigned chain seeds for each attempt.

After preparing the OCRS data, an application fit can be run with:

~~~bash
Rscript refit/applications/run_one_fit.R --arm ocrs --role Vague
Rscript refit/applications/run_one_fit.R --arm ocrs --role Vague --profile smoke --execute
~~~

This driver also supports STAR and the writing-to-learn data. It checks the prepared inputs and reads the prior and base-measure settings from the execution manifest. Use `--fit-key` to select a particular primary or sensitivity fit.

## Fit the Rasch model

The [Rasch runner](code/refit/rasch/run_one_chain.R) fits one chain using a local copy of the IRW data. For example:

~~~bash
Rscript refit/rasch/run_one_chain.R --input /path/to/gcbs_brotherton_2013_vcl.rds --arm main --role vague --attempt 1 --chain 1 --profile smoke --execute
~~~

Run the four specified chains for the same arm, role, attempt and profile. Then create a CSV with columns `chain` and `run_directory`, pointing to their completed results under `outputs/refit/rasch/`. Combine them with:

~~~bash
Rscript refit/rasch/combine_and_check.R --arm main --role vague --attempt 1 --profile smoke --index /path/to/four-chains.csv --input /path/to/gcbs_brotherton_2013_vcl.rds --execute
~~~

The [combiner](code/refit/rasch/combine_and_check.R) checks the chain identities, seeds, schedules and result hashes before pooling the draws. All chains must belong to the same attempt. Population-density calculations then use the combined draws.

## Recorded fitting checks

The November replay repeated the four selected production fits for Figure F.5 and Table F.15 on two synthetic datasets. The recorded convergence decisions, per-site posterior means and SDs, posterior mean count and site RMSE agree with the archived fits within the reported tolerance. The [replay ledger](records/provenance/selected-replay-verification.csv) identifies each fit, the original settings and the observed discrepancies.

One short four-chain synthetic simulation fit took 18.9 seconds in the November check. The September tests included a short four-chain OCRS fit (17.7 seconds), a single Rasch chain (62.4 seconds) and its conditional-density calculation. These timings include compilation and model construction and exclude installation. End-to-end combination of four newly fitted Rasch chains remains untested. The November guard tests exercised missing, duplicate and incompatible chains, repeated seeds, nonfinite draws, completed-result reuse and hash corruption. [Fitting checks](records/verification/refit-smoke.md) · [Fit status](records/provenance/refit-status.csv)

Each run records its settings, inputs, seeds, code and software hashes. `--resume --execute` checks the hash before reusing a completed result. Keep person-level latent draws produced by an optional refit in the local output directory.
